walkthroughs.body_html:
Graphic Communication — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Graphic Communication brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Graphic Communication.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CAD and CAM?
options: They are the same thing with different names.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
Repair (because it sounds eco-friendly).

mcqs.q: What does 'Rethink' mean in the 6 Rs?
options: Thinking about marketing the product.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
Questioning whether a product is necessary or could be designed differently for sustainability.
Trying a design again if it does not work first time.

mcqs.q: Which of the 6 Rs has the GREATEST environmental benefit?
options: Recycle (because it is most familiar).
Repair (because it sounds eco-friendly).
Refuse or Reduce (preventing the impact at source).
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Manufactured board”?
options: Medium-Density Fibreboard: smooth-surfaced sheet ideal for painting and machining.
Engineered wood (MDF, plywood, chipboard); uniform sheets without grain direction.
Drying timber to reduce moisture content; air or kiln seasoning.
Timber from coniferous trees (pine, spruce); fast-growing and cheaper.
